from ./Foliage import Foliage
from ./Lod import Lod
from ./Placement import Placement

export anchor Performance:
    description:
        The cost of the tree system is measured in the running game, not
        guessed. The hand-made trees are gone, so the cost is measured
        against the same stage with no trees.

    counters:
        - A tree stats overlay, shown with the @{Lod.debugView} toggle, reports per frame the number of trees drawn at each level and in a fade, the number of foliage sprites drawn, the triangles and draw calls of the tree passes, shadow passes included, and the GPU time of the tree main pass and tree shadow pass on their own.
        - It also reports the CPU time of level selection and fade updates per frame.
        - At stage load it records the time spent deriving, meshing and baking variants, how many came from the disk cache, and the GPU and disk memory the variants use.

    benchmark:
        - A benchmark runs a fixed camera path along a stage with the procedural trees and reports the average, 1% low and worst frame time, the tree GPU time and the stage load time.
        - It can run the same path with trees turned off, so the trees' own cost is the difference between the two runs.
        - Results are written to a file with the stage, graphics quality setting, resolution and GPU, so runs can be compared.

    budget:
        - The trees' cost is negligible: on the benchmark, at the game's minimum-spec GPU, 1080p and medium quality, trees add at most 1.0 ms to the average GPU frame time and at most 1.0 ms to the 1% low, compared with the same path with no trees.
        - Level selection and fade updates take at most 0.1 ms of main-thread CPU time per frame.
        - Players never wait for tree generation: with the shipped cache, trees add at most 0.5 s to a stage's load time compared with the same stage with no trees.
        - A run over budget is a failing result in the benchmark's output file.

    mitigations:
        - Foliage overdraw. Each atlas cluster image has a tight polygon of 6 to 8 vertices around its opaque part, and sprites use it instead of a full quad, so few pixels are spent on texels that fail the alpha test. Foliage sprites draw in a depth-only pass first and are then shaded only where their depth is equal, so each covered pixel is shaded once; both passes compute positions identically (@{Foliage.wind}). Sprite thinning past 120 m (@{Foliage.simplification}) cuts the sprite count of distant crowns.
        - Culling. Each frame, instances are culled against the view frustum and against a hierarchical depth buffer built from the previous frame's terrain and trees, on the GPU, and the survivors are compacted into indirect draws. A tree hidden behind a hill or a closer stand of trees costs neither vertices nor pixels.
        - Draw calls. Every impostor of every species shares one texture array and draws in a single instanced call.
        - Foliage shading. Leaf translucency is a cheap wrap-lighting term from the atlas thickness map, not a ray march or extra light lookup; ambient occlusion stays baked. No foliage shader samples more than its three atlas textures plus the shadow map.
        - Geometry. LOD0 branches of a variant have at most 6,000 triangles for a conifer or broadleaf and 2,000 for a shrub, and a crown has at most 600 sprites, 200 for a shrub.
        - Fades. At most 32 trees fade at once; a tree whose level changes while that many are fading switches at its next free slot, still with a full fade.
        - Shadows. Tree shadow casting follows @{Lod.shadows}.
        - Load. The cache is generated when the game is built and shipped with it (@{Placement.caching}).

    hotspots:
        - Alpha-tested foliage overdraw near the camera, made larger by the 120 m full-detail distance.
        - The two levels drawn together during a branch or impostor fade.
        - Shadow casters, drawn again for each cascade.
        - Stage load on a cold cache, when every variant and impostor is generated.

from ./Foliage import Foliage

export anchor Lod:
    description:
        Every variant has three levels of detail built from the same skeleton.
        Foliage does not change level: its sprites thin out continuously
        (@{Foliage.simplification}). Branch levels and the impostor change by a
        cross-fade, never a swap.

    levels:
        - LOD0 is the full skeleton as tapered branch tubes whose radial segment count falls with branch order. Twigs below a species radius are left out; the foliage sprites cover them.
        - LOD1 keeps only the trunk and the first-order limbs. The finer branches it drops sit inside the crown, so the sprites hide the change.
        - LOD2 is an octahedral impostor baked from LOD0 with its full foliage, with albedo, normal, depth and thickness, lit by the same lit path, sun, sky, fog and shadows as the geometry. It is never drawn with albedo alone.

    nesting: The levels are nested, so every segment in a coarser level is also in every finer one, in the same place and at the same radius.

    selection:
        - The level is chosen by the tree's projected height on screen, not by raw distance, so a change of camera field of view, as between the chase and the bonnet camera, picks the right level.
        - Projected height is measured from the tree's bounding sphere and the camera's position and field of view before camera shake and bounce are applied, so a shaking camera does not push trees back and forth across a threshold.
        - Each threshold has hysteresis. A tree moves to a coarser level when it drops below the threshold, and back to the finer one only when it rises above the threshold by a margin, 15% of the threshold by default.
        - The default thresholds are pushed far out, so a player near a tree only ever sees it at full detail. Sprite thinning starts below 6% of the screen height, branches move from LOD0 to LOD1 below 2.5%, and the tree moves to the impostor below 1%. For a 15 m tree at a 60 degree vertical field of view, that is roughly 215 m, 520 m and 1300 m.
        - A tree within 120 m of the camera is always drawn at LOD0 with every sprite at full size, whatever its projected height, the field of view or the graphics quality setting.
        - Selection runs once per frame per tree and depends only on that frame's camera, never on draw order, culling batches or which pass is drawing.

    transition:
        - A fade starts when the selected level changes and runs over a fixed time, 0.3 seconds by default, independent of frame rate and of how far the camera moves during it. It does not depend on where the tree is inside a distance band, so a car stopping near a threshold does not leave trees half faded.
        - Each tree keeps its own fade state, the outgoing level, the incoming level and a fade value from 0 to 1, from frame to frame. A culled tree keeps its state, and a tree that comes into view takes its selected level at once with no fade.
        - The fade value is one number per tree per frame. It is never derived from a vertex or pixel position, height, depth or texture coordinate, so a level never appears as a line or edge sweeping across the tree.
        - Both levels draw with the same screen-space dither mask and the same fade value. The outgoing level keeps the pixels whose mask value is at or above the fade value and the incoming level keeps those below it, so each pixel of the tree is covered by exactly one level and the tree is never thinner or more transparent than a solid tree at any point of the fade.
        - The dither mask is a tiled blue-noise or ordered pattern, at most 8 by 8 pixels, with no gradient or direction across the screen, anchored to screen pixels. It is not animated from frame to frame, and it is not jittered with temporal anti-aliasing unless the renderer's TAA resolves that jitter, so it does not shimmer or crawl.
        - Both levels are alpha-tested and write depth. A tree is never alpha-blended or drawn with a global opacity, so it never looks see-through while fading.
        - If the selected level changes back during a fade, the fade reverses from its current value; it never restarts from 0 or snaps. A request for a third level waits until the running fade finishes.
        - Wind sway, colour variation and lighting are the same on both levels during the fade, so nothing jumps when it ends.
        - The impostor blends the three baked views nearest the view direction by their barycentric weights, so it does not jump from view to view as the camera passes the tree.

    shadows:
        - Shadows use one level coarser than the one drawn, and never the impostor within the near shadow cascade.
        - Only the nearest shadow cascade draws trees with wind and every sprite. Farther cascades draw trees as LOD1 with thinned sprites, or the impostor, with no wind, and re-render their tree casters every fourth frame, the cascades staggered so no two re-render on the same frame.
        - Shadow casters are culled per cascade, on the GPU, like the main pass.
        - Shadow casters are never dithered. A tree's shadow level switches once, when its fade finishes, so its shadow does not flicker while the tree fades.

    budget: The thresholds, the hysteresis margin and the fade time are per species, with defaults, and the thresholds can be scaled by the graphics quality setting. Lower quality settings may bring the thresholds closer, but never inside the 120 m full-detail distance.

    debugView:
        - A debug toggle tints each tree by the level it draws, shows trees in a fade with the fade value, and marks trees that changed level more than twice in the last second, so flickering trees can be found in a running stage.
        - It can also show foliage with lighting only and with normals only, so unlit or wrongly lit sprites and impostors can be seen at once.
